problem_statement: The codrops/InteractiveColoringConcept project is a static drag-and-drop coloring workspace: a fixed color toolbar of eight draggable swatches plus a Reset colors button, a full mockup-browser website whose paintable areas and text recolor when a swatch is dropped on them, an intro overlay ('Interactive Coloring Concept') dismissed with a Got it! button, and a small shared site rail (Studio / Workflow / Plans) that links three routes of the workspace (index.html, about.html, pricing.html). A 'Palette flow' metric strip at the top of the content area is supposed to summarise the live coloring workflow (Selected palette, Applied areas, Active swatch, Reset state) on EVERY route and to reflect the visitor's actions. Three regressions are present at once. (1) Layout: the strip's four-tile metric row is a fixed non-wrapping row, so on a 390px mobile viewport it runs past the right edge and forces horizontal page overflow. (2) Continuity: the strip is wired only on the home route and was never promoted to the Workflow (about) and Plans (pricing) routes, so it disappears there. (3) Interaction: grabbing a color swatch is supposed to update the Active swatch readout to name the swatch being painted, but the readout stays 'Drag a color'. Repair all three so the strip is responsive with no horizontal overflow, is present consistently on every route, and its Active swatch readout re-renders to the swatch the visitor grabs, WITHOUT changing the strip copy, removing the color toolbar, the Reset colors control, the intro overlay, the shared site rail, or the mockup-browser website content.
required_content: Repair the Palette flow metric row so it no longer causes horizontal overflow at 390px mobile width: the document's normal-flow content must stay within the viewport (tolerance 24px), and the row must stay readable and non-overflowing on tablet and desktop where it already fits.

Promote the Palette flow strip consistently to EVERY route: it must render with its per-route modifier class palette-flow--home on index.html, palette-flow--about on about.html, and palette-flow--pricing on pricing.html, not only on the home page.

Keep the strip in the existing dark Codrops demo palette (dark #444 tiles, the #f2e0b1 eyebrow accent, compact uppercase tile labels); do not restyle the tiles into a saturated teal slab or any new visual system.

Wire the color swatches so that after the visitor grabs a swatch the Active swatch readout re-renders to 'Painting <color>' (e.g. 'Painting #333' for the first swatch); the readout must actually update on grab, not stay 'Drag a color'.
Do not remove or hide the Palette flow strip content: the Selected palette, Applied areas, Active swatch, and Reset state tiles must remain present with their live values on every route.

Keep the existing eight color swatches, the drag-and-drop paint-area coloring interaction, the Reset colors button, the intro overlay with its Got it! button, the shared Studio/Workflow/Plans site rail, and the mockup-browser website content intact.

Fix the layout, the cross-route promotion, and the readout wiring through the strip's own stylesheet and script (paletteflow-row.css and paletteflow.js), not through one-off per-element or per-page overrides.
Use source HTML/CSS/JS only; do not add dependencies, generated screenshots, remote replacement media, or iframe shortcuts.
design_constraints: Treat this as a responsive layout + cross-route continuity + interaction repair of the existing Codrops coloring demo, not as a new landing page or a redesign.
The strip must keep the existing dark demo aesthetic, the #f2e0b1 eyebrow accent, the compact uppercase tile labeling, and its placement at the top of the content area on every route.
Do not remove, rename, or hide the color toolbar, the Reset colors button, the intro overlay, the shared site rail, the mockup header/nav, or any paintable mockup section.
A narrow fixed row with overflow-x:hidden that still leaves the document wider than the viewport is NOT an acceptable repair; the metric row must genuinely wrap or shrink to fit.
The repair must be shared through the strip stylesheet and script rather than inline one-off fixes.
Avoid horizontal overflow and text overlap across desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile viewports.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the original intro overlay, coloring toolbar, site rail, and mockup shell on the home route.
tablet_initial verifies the Palette flow strip fits cleanly at tablet width.

desktop_flow and mobile_flow dismiss the intro overlay (Got it!) and verify the Palette flow strip, its four tiles, and the coloring workspace are visible; mobile_flow (and mobile_initial) verify the strip does not force horizontal overflow on a 390px viewport, and desktop_flow anchors the strip's palette/geometry.

desktop_about loads /about.html and desktop_pricing loads /pricing.html and verify the shared strip is promoted there with its palette-flow--about / palette-flow--pricing modifier and the same tile copy (cross-route continuity).
desktop_grab dismisses the overlay and grabs the first color swatch, verifying the Active swatch readout re-renders to 'Painting #333'.
desktop_reset dismisses the overlay and clicks Reset colors, verifying the reset control and Reset state tile continue to work after the repair.

change_completion: The Palette flow strip no longer overflows the 390px mobile viewport (document width within viewport, tolerance 24px) and still fits on tablet and desktop.

The strip is promoted to every route (palette-flow--about/pricing present on /about.html and /pricing.html) and the Active swatch readout re-renders on a swatch grab, all through the strip stylesheet and script.
design_consistency: The repaired strip keeps the Codrops dark demo styling (dark #444 tiles, the #f2e0b1 eyebrow accent, compact uppercase tile labeling) instead of a saturated teal slab or a new visual system.
The color toolbar, intro overlay, shared site rail, mockup header/nav, and paintable mockup sections remain intact and recognizable across routes.
responsive: The Palette flow strip and mockup remain readable at desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile widths without horizontal overflow.
The four Palette flow tiles wrap or shrink to fit narrow viewports instead of forcing the page to scroll horizontally, and stay legible without text overlap on mobile.
regression: The Interactive Coloring Concept heading, the color toolbar, the mockup website content, the Reset colors button, the shared site rail, and the intro overlay remain available.
The project continues to run as a static site with no package or build step, and the about/pricing routes keep their own titles and demo content.

metadata.design_goal: complete or refine a user workflow across one or more meaningful screens
metadata.source_repo_kind: Static Codrops interactive drag-and-drop coloring demo with a fixed color toolbar, a paintable mockup-browser website, an intro overlay, a shared site rail across three routes, and a Reset colors control.
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable interactive coloring workspace whose content area is a natural host for a Palette flow workflow strip promoted across its Studio/Workflow/Plans routes; a Repair task fixes the strip's overflow, cross-route continuity, and active-swatch readout while preserving the drag/drop coloring and reset continuity.

author_notes: Slot slot_119 targets interactive_canvas / experience_continuity / modify (Repair) / section / L4 on the codrops InteractiveColoringConcept drag-and-drop coloring demo. Although the demo is classed interactive_canvas, it is a DOM / interact.js coloring workspace with no <canvas> element, so horizontal overflow is a plain normal-flow measurement and the visual gate is anchored on the normal-flow Palette flow strip crops. The L4 lever set is orthogonal: (D6) the strip's fixed-width non-wrapping metric row overflows the 390px mobile viewport; (D2) the shared strip is promoted to every route (palette-flow--home/about/pricing) in the reference but wired home-only in the regressed legs; (D3) the reference keeps the quiet dark Codrops tile palette while the bad leg drifts to a saturated teal slab that trips block-fidelity on the strip crops; (D4) grabbing a swatch re-renders the Active swatch readout in the reference/baseline but the bad leg reads a stale closure label so the readout stays 'Drag a color'. The two leg-varying files are css/paletteflow-row.css (layout + palette) and js/paletteflow.js (cross-route promotion + readout wiring); the strip markup, shared chrome CSS, toolbar, overlay, site rail, and mockup content are identical build infrastructure across all three legs. The fixed customizer sidebar is position:fixed so it never contributes to document width; only the normal-flow strip drives the overflow gate.
